questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual is a starting point. To learn more about hazardous materials, read federal and state rules. Also attend hazardous materials training courses.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials correctly. The driver should check that materials are properly labeled.

questions.question: A person watching a placarded vehicle may be:

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.explanation: A person watching a parked placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must have a clear view of the vehicle. They cannot be in the sleeper berth.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Workers who handle hazardous materials must receive training and testing at least once every three years.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, how should you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the roadway and waving your arms.

questions.explanation: Use reflective triangles or red electric lights for warning signals. Never use flares or fuses when carrying explosives, as they can cause fires.

questions.question: If a box contains liquid containers, it must show:

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have orientation markers. Arrows on the box must point in the correct upright direction.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, what is important to know?

options.text: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to nearby packages.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to nearby packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads around each radioactive package and passes through to all nearby packages. Rules limit how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
Attach a QR code to be scanned.
Shrink the HazMat label to fit it on the item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
questions.explanation: If a diamond-shaped hazard label will not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. Only leave the engine on if you need it to run a pump.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Do not use cargo heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials. Heaters in the same space as these materials are not permitted.

questions.question: A placard indicating hazardous materials is which shape?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials may need to be:

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: When shipping papers list both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials must be identified. They can be listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in an "HM" column.

questions.question: On a shipping paper that lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials may be identified by being:
questions.explanation: When shipping papers include both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous items must be clearly identified. They can be entered first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" before the shipping description.

questions.question: Who must mark and label materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must warn drivers and others about risks. They do this by putting hazard warning labels on packages, placing placards on vehicles, and providing shipping papers and emergency response information.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually shaped like:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Many products classed as poison are also:
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials classified as poisonous are also flammable.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle:

options.text: May only be moved in an emergency.
May be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: May only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for hazardous materials on board cannot be driven, except in an emergency to protect life and property.

questions.question: The power unit of a placarded vehicle must carry a fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher with an Underwriters Laboratories (UL) rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: A placard indicating hazardous materials is shaped like a:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ away from any building.
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, place where people gather, or open fire.

questions.question: Which agency does a background check for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: When applying for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) performs a federal security threat assessment.

questions.question: What information must a shipping paper include?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers must include a description of the specific hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you may not park closer than ____ to the nearest building.
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building unless you need to stop briefly for an operational reason, like refueling.

questions.question: If your engine runs a pump for delivering compressed gas, when should you turn off the engine?
questions.explanation: If your engine runs a pump for product transfer, turn it off after the transfer is complete but before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: If you stop and leave your vehicle while carrying hazardous materials, where should the shipping papers be?

options.text: Left in the front seat of the cab.
Placed in a box under the passenger seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left in the front seat of the cab.
questions.explanation: If you leave your vehicle, the hazardous materials shipping papers must be left on the driver's seat.

questions.question: If you see a cargo leak, how should you identify the leaking hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: If you find a cargo leak, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not touch or smell leaking materials, as this could cause injury or death.

questions.question: What information must a shipping paper include?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the planned route.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must list an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: How should a shipper warn others about hazardous materials?

options.text: Posting HazMat placards on their truck.
Putting flashing lights on their truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Posting HazMat placards on their truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers of certain hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on transporting vehicles. Shippers must provide placards, labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, where should placards be placed?

options.text: Should be used on all four sides of the vehicle.
Should be used only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When required, hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
